episode_title: Lessons From an Outdoor Living Builder Who Almost Shut It All Down | Casey Laughlin of Texas Outdoor Oasis
question: How did Texas Outdoor Oasis revenue grow from near zero to $1 million in the first year after Casey Laughlin's 2010 acquisition?
transcript_excerpt: Marketing had almost everything to do with it. Laughlin recognized a huge influx of new business moving into the Frisco, Allen, and McKinney areas as State Farm was building a headquarters and bringing people from California and out of state. There was no saturation of outdoor living companies at that point, so they took quick advantage of the market and scaled rapidly.

episode_title: Lessons From an Outdoor Living Builder Who Almost Shut It All Down | Casey Laughlin of Texas Outdoor Oasis
question: What happened when Casey Laughlin's original Texas Outdoor Oasis designer disappeared with project plans in 2012?
transcript_excerpt: The designer walked off with plans for a six-figure project, thinking he could take it and put himself back in business. Laughlin had not educated himself on the business operations and had no backup plan, so he instructed his secretary to refund all customers their 50% deposits and shut the construction division down before being introduced to Tommy Redfern.

episode_title: Lessons From an Outdoor Living Builder Who Almost Shut It All Down | Casey Laughlin of Texas Outdoor Oasis
question: How did Tommy Redfern change Texas Outdoor Oasis' approach from competing on price to building on quality?
transcript_excerpt: Tommy taught Laughlin a different mindset by shifting from quantity versus quality. When they switched to tongue and groove finish with high detail work, their price ran about $6 higher than competitors, but they began selling consistently. Tommy convinced Laughlin that if quality is there, people will buy it, and this philosophy increased their project margins and reputation.

episode_title: Lessons From an Outdoor Living Builder Who Almost Shut It All Down | Casey Laughlin of Texas Outdoor Oasis
question: What major failure in 2017 cost Texas Outdoor Oasis enough money to have funded all subsequent PHTA training for their team?
transcript_excerpt: When Laughlin started building pools in 2017, the company had a major failure that year which cost them significant money—enough to have paid for all the PHTA (Pool Hot Tub Alliance) training he later invested in for his team. This taught him that early training investment could have prevented costly pitfalls from doing things wrong.

episode_title: Lessons From an Outdoor Living Builder Who Almost Shut It All Down | Casey Laughlin of Texas Outdoor Oasis
question: Why did Pentair's operating platform for pool builders shut down in December 2024 after Texas Outdoor Oasis invested months building it out?
transcript_excerpt: In July 2024, Laughlin signed on to use Pentair's custom-built operating platform designed specifically for pool builders using Pentair equipment. The team spent five months building it out and was set to launch on January 1, but on December 20th they received an email that Pentair pulled the plug on the entire program, resulting in wasted time and a major setback.
